title: IMAT Chemistry Question Bank 2011-2024
note: Official past-exam questions: for private teaching/analysis only, NOT for verbatim inclusion in shipped/paid products. 2025 added 2026-08-14: transcribed from the AcadIMAT shuffled paper; answers independently solved, then verified 15/15 against the official key.

years.notes: Chemistry section is Q59-69 (11 questions). Q59 is a table question; each option row is rendered as 'K to Ca: ...; Sc to Zn: ...; Ga to Br: ...'. Q64 contains a partial Periodic Table figure; the element positions shown are transcribed in brackets in the question text. Superscript charges in Q65 verified against page images.

Chemistry section is Q59-69 (11 questions). pdftotext rendered superscript minus signs as soft hyphens; fixed to ASCII (e.g. I-, ClO4-). Q66 contains a partial Periodic Table figure; element positions transcribed in brackets from the page image. Q68 is a table question; each row rendered inline in the question text. Q61: the second equation appears in the original exam as '2Fe3+(aq) + 2I-(aq) → Fe2+(aq) + I2(aq)' (Fe2+ printed without the coefficient 2, verified against page image); kept verbatim.

Chemistry section is Q45-52 (only 8 questions; the 2013 exam has 60 questions total, fewer science items than 2011-2012). Page footers in the 2013 exam PDF read '(c) UCLES 2012' - an artifact of the original paper, not a file mix-up (question numbering and answer key match). Q46's synthesis-route scheme transcribed as text from the page image. Q49 contains a full outline Periodic Table figure of the main group elements with symbols shown; described in brackets.

Chemistry section contains only 10 questions (43-52), fewer than the typical 12-15. Q51: reaction scheme is a diagram; transcribed from a page image into bracketed text. Q52: the substance list and option formulas were images in the text layer; transcribed from a page image. All answers verified against the key by question number.

Q43: the self-ionisation equation was an image; transcribed from a page image as H2O(l) <=> H+(aq) + OH-(aq). Q44: the exam's printed font renders 1s as 'Is' (e.g. Is22s22p6...); normalized to standard 1s2 2s2 ... notation with spaces added between subshells for ASCII readability. Soft hyphens in the extraction (e.g. 1-bromopropane, propan-1-ol) replaced with normal hyphens. All answers verified against the key by question number.

Q45: the equilibrium equation was an image; transcribed from a page image as CH3OH(l) + CH3COOH(l) <=> CH3COOCH3(l) + H2O(l), dH = -8.5 kJ/mol. Q50: the ion symbol was an image; it is Cr3+ with mass number 52 and atomic number 24, written [52/24]Cr3+. Q52: the five vanadium ion charges were superscript images that collide in plain ASCII; caret notation used to disambiguate (VO3^- means the VO3 ion with charge 1-, VO^2+ means the VO ion with charge 2+, VO2^+ means the VO2 ion with charge 1+). Q44: the leading numbers in the particle list (12Mg2+, 10Ne, 16S2-, 9F-, 3Li+) are printed atomic-number subscripts. All answers verified against the key by question number.

Chemistry section is Q41-52 (12 questions). Q42, Q43, and Q52 contain typeset symbols/equations that pdftotext dropped; those pages were rendered as images and transcribed. Nuclide notation written as mass/atomic-number prefix, e.g. 16/8 O2- means mass number 16, atomic number 8. Key extracted cleanly as text.

Chemistry section is Q41-52 (12 questions). Q43 and Q46 reference skeletal-structure figures (transcribed descriptions included, [FIGURE] noted). Q44, Q45 use nuclide/subscript notation dropped by pdftotext; pages rendered as images and transcribed. Q47 contains a 5-row table, transcribed inline. Nuclide notation written as mass/atomic-number prefix, e.g. 23/11 Z. Key extracted cleanly as text.
Chemistry section is questions 41-52 (12 questions). Clean text extraction, no figures. All answers matched from key by question number.

Chemistry section is questions 41-52 (12 questions). Q46, Q47 and Q49 contain figures that pdftotext dropped; pages 27-29 were rendered to images and the figures transcribed into the question text (Q46 structures transcribed as condensed/skeletal descriptions, Q47 Kc expression written in plain ASCII, Q49 cysteine structure transcribed as HS-CH2-CH(NH2)-COOH). All answers matched from key by question number.

Exam PDF is image-based; all questions transcribed from page renders (pages 21-25, Chemistry section Q41-52). Q44 references three displayed structural formulas (transcribed as descriptions in [FIGURE]). Q46 shows the displayed structure of vitamin B5 ([FIGURE]). Q48 shows displayed structures of AlCl3 and Al2Cl6 plus a 5-row table (table transcribed as text). Superscripts in Q42 electron configurations written as plain digits after orbital letters (e.g. 1s2 2s2 2p6).

Exam PDF is image-based; all questions transcribed from page renders (pages 19-23, Chemistry section Q36-50). Q38 references a displayed triglyceride + 3X -> 3Y + glycerol scheme ([FIGURE], transcribed). Q40 uses isotope notation, rendered as mass/atomic number prefixes (e.g. 79/35 Br-). Q48 table transcribed as text. Possible key anomaly: Q41 key answer A ('1 and 2 only', i.e. BF3 and NH4+) excludes CO2, though carbon in CO2 also shares all 4 outer-shell electrons; answer recorded from key as instructed.

Exam PDF is image-based; all questions transcribed from 120dpi page renders (pages 11-14). Chemistry section runs Q33-47 (15 questions), between Biology (ends Q32) and Physics and Mathematics (starts Q48). Q33 uses nuclide notation rendered inline as text here. Q37, Q41, and Q47 contain structure drawings, replaced with [FIGURE: ...] descriptions of the drawn structures. Q34 and Q46 options are typeset fractions, linearized with parentheses.

Exam PDF is image-based; all questions transcribed from 120dpi page renders (pages 7-9). Chemistry section runs Q33-47 (15 questions), before Physics and Mathematics (starts Q48). In the shuffled PDF, Q33 renders as 'a pressure of 2.4 atm 222 on the walls' - the stray '222' is drifted subscript digits from N2, CO2 and O2; cross-checked against the original unshuffled 2024 exam, which reads '0.3 mol of N2, 0.5 mol of CO2, and 0.4 mol of O2 exerts a pressure of 2.4 atm'. Transcribed with corrected formulas.

questions.text: A sealed container contains 1.00 mol of hydrogen gas, which behaves as an ideal gas. Which of the following changes increase(s) the total kinetic energy of the hydrogen gas molecules initially within the container? 1. Changing the amount of hydrogen from 1.0 mol to 1.2 mol whilst keeping the pressure and volume constant. 2. Changing the pressure from 1.0 atm to 1.2 atm whilst keeping the volume and number of moles constant. 3. Changing the volume from 1.0 L to 1.2 L whilst keeping the pressure and number of moles constant.

When nitrogen and hydrogen are mixed under suitable conditions of temperature and pressure, and in the presence of a catalyst, an equilibrium state is attained: N2(g) + 3H2(g) <=> 2NH3(g)  Delta H is negative. Which of the following statements explain(s) why, when the pressure on a mixture of nitrogen and hydrogen is increased while the temperature remains constant, the time taken to attain equilibrium is decreased? 1. The molecules have a higher collision frequency. 2. The yield of ammonia (NH3(g)) decreases. 3. A greater proportion of molecules in the mixture have energy greater than the activation energy.

Which of the following statements, if any, are correct for the properties of Group I elements? 1. They form hydrides where the hydrogen has an oxidation state of -1. 2. They can reduce iodine to iodide. 3. Their outer electrons are delocalised when in the liquid state.

A student observed that when powdered sugar at -1 degrees C was added to ice at -1 degrees C all of the ice melted. Which of the following statements explain this observation? 1 Sugar has given the water molecules energy. 2 The melting point of the mixture is higher. 3 The melting point of the mixture is lower.
Which of the following equations represent(s) a redox reaction? 1 4LiH + AlCl3 -> 3LiCl + LiAlH4  2 N2O3 + 3H2O -> 2H3O+ + 2NO2-  3 NH4NO3 -> 2H2O + N2O

Consider the following reversible reaction at temperature T. A + 2B <=> 2C + D. At equilibrium, there are 0.5 moles of A, 0.2 moles of B, 0.5 moles of C and 0.8 moles of D, all in a vessel of volume V. What is the value of the equilibrium constant, Kc, at this temperature?

A compound consists of carbon, hydrogen and oxygen only. 8 g of this compound contains 3 g of carbon and 1 g of hydrogen. Which one of the following could be the molecular formula of the compound? [Ar values: C = 12; H = 1; O = 16]
Why does hydrogen iodide (HI) have a higher boiling point than hydrogen bromide (HBr)? [Atomic numbers: bromine = 35; iodine = 53]

options.A: The iodide ions in HI are larger than the bromide ions in HBr.
options.B: The H-I covalent bond is stronger than the H-Br covalent bond.
options.C: There are hydrogen bonds between HI molecules but not between HBr molecules.
options.D: The permanent dipole-permanent dipole forces between HI molecules are stronger than those between HBr molecules.
options.E: The induced dipole-induced dipole (dispersion) forces between HI molecules are stronger than those between HBr molecules.
